description: Two words in this verse ask something of us. Depending is not the same as managing, and searching is not the same as hoping.
excerpt: Most of the time I'm not really depending. I'm managing. Handling. Capable. Asking Him to help me pull off my own plan instead of asking Him what His plan actually is.
verse: "The Lord is good to those who depend on him, to those who search for him."
body_html:
Two questions come out of this verse when I read it.

Do I actually depend on God? And do I actually search for Him?

Not do I say I do. Not do I want to. Actually do it.

Depending on God and searching for God aren't passive things. They require something of me. Depending means I'm not carrying it myself. When the hard thing shows up, my default isn't scrambling for my own solutions. My first move is to bring it to Him, not figure it out and then ask Him to bless what I already decided.

Most of the time I'm not really depending. I'm managing. Handling. Capable. Asking Him to help me pull off my own plan instead of asking Him what His plan actually is.

Searching looks the same way. It means actively looking for Him. In His Word. Quiet enough to hear Him. Paying attention to where He's already at work. Not waiting for Him to shout at me from the sky, but going after Him.

A lot of us aren't searching. We're hoping. Hoping He'll show up, that we'll feel Him, that something will click. But the promise here isn't for the hopeful. It's for the ones who depend and the ones who search.

The Lord is good to those people.

That means the goodness of God being poured out on our lives isn't disconnected from what we're doing on our end. If I want to experience Him as good, and not just believe He's good in theory, I have to actually depend on Him and actually search for Him.

Am I depending, or just performing? Am I searching, or just waiting?

Which of those two words feels like the one God is inviting you into right now?
question: Which of those two words feels like the one God is inviting you into right now?
